body:
Records the unrefereed claim **C₈₂ < 0.253091834***, preserves historical bounds, and updates the README bound and recent progress.

This replaces the 0.253123275 first filed here. The construction and proof are the same. A second search run added three degree-44 denominators and regenerated the numerators. It stopped by a preset rule when gains slowed, so this says nothing about optimality.

This is the same limit-point construction, with new denominator factors. PR #280 kept seven known denominator factors and changed the numerators. Here eight new monic degree-44 denominators replace most of them, found with a complementary-measure IRLS/CVP search, and the numerators are regenerated against the moved LP dual. The certificate has 9 denominator factors and 47 numerator factors, most of them new, with D = 1,000,000,000,064.

The strongest earlier bound I found is PR #280 by vidigoat, 0.2534350402, which is still open. This builds on it: the numerator search is its iterated LLL method, and I reproduced its LP and verified its certificate before starting. Credit also to Doche for the formula and factors, Grinsztajn for factors, and Épi for Ed5 and unequal multiplicities. No exhaustive priority or optimality is claimed.

Certificate, checkers and receipts: https://github.com/rpinho/c82-height-certificate/tree/6d4e80cb0b375c767df91eae7985ae3e8bef7203/degree44-denominators-v2. The proof is in the sibling folder degree44-denominators at the same commit, and doesn't depend on which factors are used. The checker imports no search code, is unchanged from the first filing, and gives the rigorous upper endpoint 0.25309183355151 at 256 bits.

The separate integrator from the AI review shares no code with it and gives the numerical estimate 0.25309183355146. Correction (4 Nov): earlier text presented the review integrator's 0.25309183355146 next to the endpoint; it is not an upper bound. The true value is about 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁵ above it, as an [independent replay](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/301#issuecomment-6628606867) by arhancanli pointed out. Only the checker's 0.25309183355151 is a rigorous upper end, and the bound 0.253091834 is unchanged. The certificate README now says this ([math-certificates c82](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/c356b145e936c6d121a1319ae5ece97c716e0bff/c82/degree44-denominators-v2/README.md)). The exact algebra audit rechecked all 423 coprimality pairs. These were rerun by the same agents, with no new review, so that isn't a second party and the asterisk stays.

AI use and author review: Analysis and proof drafting by AI agents under my direction; I reviewed the results at summary level. AI agents also prepared the certificate, checkers and submission text. This does not claim a line-by-line human verification.

**Verification level: L0** for the bound as a whole: the new integration and error bounds on the inherited Doche reduction are reviewed only in prose; a reviewer wrote a separate complete checker of the certificate, but different-model or different-party provenance is not established (definitions: https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/59eeb7097f806da05187b5f234445be3589204d4/VERIFICATION_LEVELS.md). The replay above was posted after this level was set and is not yet reflected in it.
